subject.title: fix(memory-core): WAL checkpoint after writeMeta + stale index file cleanup

question: Should memory-core require a checked live WAL checkpoint before this PR can merge, or may the post-publish checkpoint remain best-effort?
rationale: The code location is plausible, but accepting a best-effort checkpoint is a durability and availability tradeoff that green CI cannot settle.

options.title: Require checked checkpoint semantics
options.body: Read the wal_checkpoint result row, warn/retry/fail on busy or incomplete frames, and add regression proof for that path before merge.

options.title: Accept best-effort checkpointing
options.body: Maintainers may accept the lighter patch, but the PR body and tests should stop claiming guaranteed metadata durability before close.

options.title: Coordinate with safe-reindex work
options.body: Pause this branch until the broader read-latch PR lands or is explicitly replaced, then rebase the WAL durability fix on the final lifecycle shape.

recommendation.title: Require checked checkpoint semantics
recommendation.body: Read the wal_checkpoint result row, warn/retry/fail on busy or incomplete frames, and add regression proof for that path before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent per-agent SQLite and memory publish/reindex history makes vincentkoc the strongest available routing candidate for the durability tradeoff.
